text:
Elena: Heads-up, escalated from an enterprise customer — they're seeing very high tail latencies (p95 -> p999) on the embeddings endpoint during bursty traffic. They also intermittently get a 422 "Dimension mismatch" and one occurrence of a 500 from the batcher. Repro window: Monday 09:42-09:55 UTC.

Sam: Can you paste the raw error lines and the config for the deployment (max_batch_size/dynamic batching settings)? Also, which model variant are they hitting?

Elena: Logs pasted below. Model: embed-ada-1536-v2 (customer pinned). Routing: hosted-us-east. Config snippet from our console for that deployment: 

```
batching: {
  dynamic: true,
  max_batch_size: 128,
  target_latency_ms: 20,
  timeout_ms: 50,
  enable_padding: true
}
```

Error lines from the runtime (scrubbed):

```
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [batcher] queued=312 inflight=4 forming_batch size=128 wait_ms=49
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [batcher] created batch id=0 size=128 padded_to=128
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [runtime] model_request id=0 start -> model call
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [runtime] model response id=0 status=200 dim=1536
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [batcher] created batch id=1 size=56 padded_to=128
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [runtime] model_request id=1 start -> model call
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [runtime] model response id=1 status=500 error="internal: kernel mismatch"
[2026-03-09T09:43:12Z] [ingress] reply id=1 to client status=422 error="DimMismatch: expected 1536 got 0"
```

Priya: Couple hypotheses based on that trace: 1) The 500 in the model path caused the second smaller batch to go to a fallback code path that returned an empty vector (hence dim=0), and our ingress layer converted that into a 422 for the client. 2) The dynamic batching and padding are creating very large batches (max_batch_size=128) so when a batch fails we amplify the blast radius and increase retry/backoff pressure -> tail latency spikes.

Sam: That lines up. Also the logs show a long queued=312 — suggests the customer's traffic was spiky and our batcher was waiting to fill batches up to 128 before flush. That pushes many requests into a single batch and increases p99/p999 when anything in the batch goes slow or errors.

Priya: Repro steps I ran locally to simulate the burst (useful for SEs):

1) Quick k6 style burst script (we used curl to emulate):
```bash
for i in {1..300}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"embed-ada-1536-v2","input":["short text $i"]}' &
done
wait
```

2) Observe batcher logs and p95/p99. With max_batch_size=128 and timeout_ms=50 we reproduced tail spikes (~3-6x p99 vs baseline) and occasional 500s from the model when batched >96 (local repro shows instability around 120).

Sam: Nice repro. Actionable mitigations (short-term):
- Reduce max_batch_size for that deployment from 128 -> 32 (or 16) to reduce amplification.
- Lower timeout_ms to 10-20ms so batches flush earlier.
- Disable padding (enable_padding=false) to avoid sending large padded tensors when the model implementation has issues with padded batches.
- Add a per-client concurrency cap / rate limiting to avoid single tenant filling the queue.

Priya: Longer-term: the runtime should detect model 500s originating from kernel mismatches and avoid returning empty vectors. We should:
- Add a safe-fallback that returns per-request 5xx instead of silently producing zero-dim vectors.
- Add a batch-level circuit breaker so if model returns an internal error for a batch we mark the model instance and try alternate instance/variant before replying.
- Track per-batch size vs model error rates (histogram) to detect thresholds where model instability rises.

Elena: For the customer, I proposed these immediate changes and sent a canary: set max_batch_size=32, timeout_ms=15, enable_padding=false for their deployment; also turned on per-tenant qps cap at 200rps. Will monitor.

OpsBot: Deploy change succeeded to customer-deploy-123 (revision 2026-03-09T10:01Z).

Sam: Let's also gather the raw request bodies from the customer's client (timestamps) to confirm they aren't sending mixed input types (e.g., sometimes arrays of floats vs strings). Dimension mismatch sometimes is client-side (expecting previous model dim). Ask SE to confirm their client SDK version.

Priya: Quick sanity checks we ran:
- Sent mixed payloads (some with arrays as inputs, some with text) -> batcher accepts mixed input types but model quantization path hits a bug when padding is enabled and sequences are empty. Repro note: if model gets an all-empty padded batch we saw dim=0.

Elena: Customer responded: their SDK was pinned to an older client that assumed dim=1024. They updated to latest SDK and will retest. Also they acknowledged heavy burst pattern due to background job.

Sam: Follow-ups for eng-runtime team: (1) Add a safety check in ingress to never return zero-dim as a success — convert to 5xx. (2) Telemetry: per-batch size + model error correlation dashboard. (3) Consider adaptive batch sizing: if error rate jumps with larger batches, automatically reduce max_batch_size for that model pool.

Priya: I'll open a runtime GH issue with repro script, logs, and a small harness that flips max_batch_size and measures p99.

Elena: Customer reports latency back to normal after canary changes (p99 back to baseline, no more 422s during the observation window). Closing for now but leaving runtime action items open.

Sam: Great. If anyone on-call sees recurring dim-mismatch, ping me + Priya.

Elena: Thx everyone. :thumbsup:
